relations.subject: tool:couchbase-cli-setting-alert
relations.evidence: This command is used to set up email alerts on a cluster.

relations.subject: tool:couchbase-cli-setting-alert
relations.evidence: Specifies the username of the user executing the command. If you do not have a user account with permission to execute the command then it will fail with an unauthorized error.

relations.subject: tool:couchbase-cli-setting-alert
relations.evidence: This tool supports authenticating against a Couchbase Cluster by using certificate based authentication (mTLS authentication).

relations.subject: tool:couchbase-cli-setting-alert
relations.evidence: An encrypted PKCS#12 certificate/key may be provided using: - `--client-cert <path>`\- `--client-cert-password <password>`

notable_absence.finding: The DESCRIPTION and OPTIONS list a specific, closed set of --alert-* flags (auto-failover node/max/node-down/cluster-small/disable, ip-changed, disk-space, meta-overhead, meta-oom, write-failed, audit-msg-dropped, indexer-max-ram, timestamp-drift-exceeded, node-time, disk-analyzer, memory-threshold, bucket-history-size, indexer-low-resident-percentage, memcached-connections) but this is never modeled as a formal enum anywhere on the page - each is its own boolean flag with its own prose sentence, several near-duplicates of each other in phrasing ('Specifies that an email alert should be sent when...'). More telling for this round's authorship-provenance angle: --alert-communication-issue is documented in full under OPTIONS ('Specifies that an email alert should be sent when nodes are experiencing communication issues.') but is completely absent from the SYNOPSIS flag list at the top of the page - a flag whose OPTIONS entry exists but whose SYNOPSIS entry was never added or was dropped, exactly the kind of terse, unreviewed drift the round's provenance hypothesis predicts for engineer-maintained CLI pages.

cross_component_finding: Every permission-gated flag on this page (username/password auth) is covered only by the generic boilerplate sentence 'If you do not have a user account with permission to execute the command then it will fail with an unauthorized error' - the page never names a specific role or privilege (no role:administrator, no cluster.settings!write style privilege string). This boilerplate recurs verbatim across the whole batch of setting-* subcommand pages read for this round, and stands in contrast to how other rounds have found the REST API and RBAC reference pages naming concrete roles/privileges for equivalent settings endpoints - the CLI reference never bridges from 'unauthorized error' down to the actual role:/privilege: catalogue.
cross_product_finding: Not directly evidenced on this page; see the couchbase-cli.md overview record for the batch-level finding on the CLI's own self-described authentication model versus how other rounds have documented the equivalent REST API / Web Console surface.
